You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE museum (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Num_of_Staff INT,
    Open_Year TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visitor (
    ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Level_of_membership INT,
    Age INT,
    UNIQUE (ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visit (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    visitor_ID TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Num_of_Ticket INT,
    Total_spent REAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (visitor_ID) REFERENCES visitor(ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Museum_ID) REFERENCES museum(Museum_ID)
);

To get **frequent museum visitors**, we first need to define “frequent.” Common meanings:

### Option 1) Visitors who made the most visits (top N)
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(*) AS num_visits
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
ORDER BY num_visits DESC;
```

### Option 2) Visitors with at least X visits (e.g., 3+)
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(*) AS num_visits
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
ORDER BY num_visits DESC;
```

### Option 3) Frequent visitors per museum (who visits each museum most)
```sql
SELECT
  m.Museum_ID,
  m.Name AS museum_name,
  v.ID AS visitor_id,
  v.Name AS visitor_name,
  COUNT(*) AS num_visits
FROM visit vi
JOIN museum m ON m.Museum_ID = vi.Museum_ID
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
GROUP BY m.Museum_ID, m.Name, v.ID, v.Name
ORDER BY m.Museum_ID, num_visits DESC;
```

Which definition do you want (top N overall, threshold like 3+, or per museum), and what number should we use (e.g., top 10 or 5+ visits)?
we should look at visitors who went to museums more than once.

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(*) AS num_visits
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY num_visits DESC, v.ID;
```
also need to think about people who visited these museums.

If you mean: **for each museum, list the visitors who visited that same museum more than once**, use:

```sql
SELECT
  m.Museum_ID,
  m.Name AS museum_name,
  v.ID AS visitor_id,
  v.Name AS visitor_name,
  COUNT(*) AS num_visits
FROM visit vi
JOIN museum  m ON m.Museum_ID = vi.Museum_ID
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
GROUP BY m.Museum_ID, m.Name, v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY m.Museum_ID, num_visits DESC, v.ID;
```

Or if you mean: **show everyone who visited any museum that has repeat visitors** (even if they themselves only came once), tell me and I’ll adjust.
we need to get the unique IDs of those visitors too.

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  vi.visitor_ID
FROM visit vi
GROUP BY vi.visitor_ID
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
```

If you want the unique visitor IDs **per museum** (repeat visitors to the same museum):

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  vi.Museum_ID,
  vi.visitor_ID
FROM visit vi
GROUP BY vi.Museum_ID, vi.visitor_ID
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
```
also need to get the names of these visitors

To get the **unique IDs and names** of visitors who visited **more than once**:

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY v.ID;
```

If you mean “visited the **same museum** more than once”:

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY v.ID;
```
We should focus on visitors who specifically went to museums.

To focus on **visitors who went to (at least one) museum** (i.e., appear in `visit`), and return their **unique IDs and names**:

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  v.ID,
  v.Name
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
ORDER BY v.ID;
```
we should also get the ages of the visitors along with their details

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  v.Age,
  v.Level_of_membership
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
ORDER BY v.ID;
```
